clue.text: Those enforcing rules in crapulent lager tours

blocks.note: the ten letters to be rearranged

clue.text: Women's undies hang on line occasionally

indicators.note: occasionally means now and then, so only every other letter of the word is kept

blocks.note: second and fourth letters of the word

explanation.surface: Instructions for drying underwear: peg the knickers out on the washing line now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: Lingerie is the collective word for women's underwear and nightclothes.

clue.text: Aussie statesman in the thrall of fab bottoms

indicators.note: held captive inside the following words, so the answer sits within them

blocks.note: the run of letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: An Australian politician besotted with shapely rear ends.
explanation.walkthrough: Tony Abbott was Prime Minister of Australia from 2013 to 2015.
explanation.definitionFit: Tony Abbott, former Australian Prime Minister, is a statesman from Australia.

clue.text: Hip apartment English separatist leader blows up

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

explanation.surface: A trendy flat owned by a radical English nationalist goes up in smoke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blows up' suggests an explosion, but here it means pumps full of air.
explanation.definitionFit: To inflate something is to blow it up with air or gas, like a balloon.

clue.text: A protest to get rid of love will be hopeless

indicators.note: getting rid of something means removing it, so a letter is dropped

blocks.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A lovers' tiff in which protesting against romance is doomed to fail.
explanation.walkthrough: Love is the tennis score for zero, which looks like the letter O, a standard crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Abject describes a wretched, hopeless state, as in abject poverty or abject failure.

clue.text: Republican to cut support for one bearing crown

indicators.note: a cut goes into something, so one piece is pushed inside another

blocks.note: a golf tee supports the ball

explanation.surface: A Republican plans to slash funding for the monarchy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one bearing crown' suggests a king or queen; the crown is the leafy top of a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: A tree's crown is its spreading canopy of branches and leaves, so a tree carries one.

clue.text: Abominable type is still child at heart

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its centre, so only the middle letter is kept

blocks.note: the central letter of the five

explanation.surface: A dreadful sort who remains a kid deep down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abominable' is not an insult here: the yeti is the Abominable Snowman of the Himalayas.
explanation.definitionFit: The yeti is popularly called the Abominable Snowman, a legendary ape-like creature.

clue.text: Late boozer having last of Guinness in a jug…

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter, which alone is kept

blocks.note: a boozer is British slang for a pub

explanation.surface: A tardy drinker taking the dregs of his stout from a jug, continued in the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: A jug is slang for prison, so 'in a jug' means imprisoned, not holding beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Behind bars is an idiom for being locked up in prison, which 'jug' also means in slang.

clue.text: Wooden sort of box purloined by heroin addict

indicators.note: something purloined is taken and held by the thief, so one piece ends up inside the others

blocks.note: a chest is a large box
a nut is an enthusiast or fanatic

explanation.surface: A wooden box of some kind is pinched by a drug user.
explanation.walkthrough: The heroin and addict pair up around the box.
explanation.definitionFit: The horse chestnut is a tree, so a type of wood-producing plant, the source of conkers.

clue.text: …overeager to be seen in Tulungagung hostelry

indicators.note: the answer can be seen lying inside the following words

blocks.note: the run of letters spanning the end of the town and the start of the next word

explanation.walkthrough: Tulungagung is a town in East Java, Indonesia, chosen for its helpful ending.
explanation.definitionFit: Gung-ho means excessively enthusiastic or zealous, often recklessly so.

clue.text: Freed soldiers told stories about victory in Europe

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the story-telling goes round the victory

blocks.note: VE Day marked victory in Europe in 1945

explanation.surface: Liberated troops recounted war tales of the Allied triumph in Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: To be relieved of a burden or duty is to be freed from it.

clue.text: Surrealist painter seen with Stones visiting China

indicators.note: a visitor goes inside someone's home, so one piece enters the other

blocks.note: first part of the friend word

explanation.surface: An artist photographed with the Rolling Stones on their tour of China.
explanation.walkthrough: China is Cockney rhyming slang for mate (china plate = mate); GRIT goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: René Magritte was a Belgian painter, a leading figure of the Surrealist movement.

clue.text: Primarily tense individual smacks heavyweights

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter is kept

blocks.note: I is one, a single individual
to tan someone's hide is to beat them

explanation.surface: A nervy person lands blows on some big bruisers.
explanation.definitionFit: Titans are figures of great power or importance, after the giant gods of Greek myth.

clue.text: Model in car possibly about to crash on trail

blocks.note: nodding off, on the verge of falling asleep; to crash is to sleep
to dog someone is to follow them

explanation.surface: A car crash looms for someone on a mountain trail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crash' suggests a collision but is slang for falling asleep. A nodding dog is a toy dog whose head bobs, set on a car's rear shelf.
explanation.definitionFit: The nodding dog is a small ornamental figure traditionally displayed in a car's rear window.

clue.text: Ending that son ruined in Brief Encounter?

explanation.surface: A film critic complaining that a son character spoiled the ending of the classic 1945 film.
explanation.walkthrough: Brief Encounter is a famous David Lean film of unconsummated romance; the question mark admits the definition is playful.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-night stand is a sexual liaison lasting a single night, literally a brief romantic encounter.

clue.text: Private or subordinate mistaking Foxtrot for Tango

indicators.note: mistaking one thing for another puts the wrong one in its place, so a letter is swapped

blocks.note: F in the NATO phonetic alphabet
T in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An army private or junior who muddles up two dances on the parade ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Private' looks like a soldier, but means inner or hidden, as in interior thoughts.
explanation.definitionFit: Interior means inner or internal, hence private as opposed to outward or public.

clue.text: Deal aide put into action in city abroad

indicators.note: putting something into action sets it moving, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A trade envoy is deployed to close a deal in a foreign city.
explanation.definitionFit: Adelaide is the capital of South Australia, an overseas city from a British view.

clue.text: Paul McCartney is one ditching the intro in Help!

indicators.note: ditching the intro means dropping the opening, so the first letter goes

blocks.note: McCartney played bass guitar in the Beatles

clue.text: Corrupt politician you slapped in anger

blocks.note: start of the word for anger
end of the word for anger, ire

clue.text: Nervous cast outside opening of Inception or Memento

cast means thrown or moulded afresh, so the letters are reshaped
the reshaped word sits on the outside, wrapping round the kept letter

explanation.walkthrough: Inception and Memento are both Christopher Nolan films; the second is the definition, as a common noun.

clue.text: Amphetamines found in part of Oxford and Sweden

explanation.walkthrough: 'Oxford' suggests the city, but an Oxford is a style of shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: Uppers is slang for stimulant drugs, especially amphetamines, that lift mood.

clue.text: Tea and a slice of orange knight gets escort

indicators.note: a slice is a single piece cut off, here just the opening letter of the fruit

blocks.note: char or cha is British slang for tea
'a' as in so much a head, i.e. per
N is the knight in chess notation

explanation.surface: A knight is served afternoon tea and orange slices before accompanying a lady.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'a' does double service in the surface; in the wordplay 'and a' simply adds PER, meaning each.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaperon accompanies and supervises someone, typically a young woman, in public: an escort.

clue.text: Short gangster getting time is amusing individual

explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone a hoot means they are hilarious, a source of great fun.

clue.text: Accidents Putin initially called suspicious at front

clue.text: Worked up or set for bed?

clue.text: Bit of rain in desert

blocks.note: second meaning: to abandon or leave

explanation.surface: A rare shower falls in an arid wilderness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'desert' looks like the sandy noun, but it is the verb, to abandon.
